items.question: Which recommendation means an immediate landing without delay?
items.explanation: “LAND IMMEDIATELY” = self explanatory, landing without delay.

items.question: Which recommendation requires landing at the nearest site at which a safe landing can be made?
items.explanation: “LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE” = urgent, nearest safe landing site.

items.question: Which recommendation allows the pilot to proceed to the nearest airfield where assistance is available?
items.explanation: “LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE” = less urgent, nearest airfield where assistance can be expected.

items.question: Which recommendation means the flight can be continued to the destination?
items.explanation: “CONTINUE FLIGHT” = flight as planned, repair at destination.

items.question: What happens when the [HORN] pushbutton on the SCU is pressed?
items.explanation: Pressing [HORN] activates the audio warning.

items.question: What happens when a red warning appears on the warning panel?
items.explanation: A gong is generated for each red warning.

items.question: At what rotor speed (Nr) is a 310 Hz continuous tone heard?
items.explanation: Continuous 310 Hz tone is heard when Nr < 360 rpm.

items.question: An intermittent 310 Hz tone is heard when:
items.explanation: Intermittent 310 Hz tone is heard when Nr > 410 rpm.

items.question: If you experience an engine flame-out in cruise flight, what are the first three immediate actions?
options: Reduce collective, set IAS Vy, twist grip to IDLE
Reduce collective, pedals adjust, cyclic forward
Twist grip IDLE, cyclic flare, collective increase
Cyclic flare, adjust pedals, rotor brake apply
items.explanation: The three first steps: Collective – reduce, IAS – Vy, Twist grip – IDLE.

items.question: During autorotation after flame-out, what control action is required at approximately 70 ft (21 m)?
items.explanation: At 70 ft the cyclic must be flared to reduce descent and speed before touchdown.

items.question: At 20–25 ft (6–8 m), which of the following is not part of the recommended procedure?
items.explanation: At 20–25 ft: increase collective gradually, cyclic forward to slight nose-up (<10°), adjust pedals. Full low pitch is only after the aircraft has stopped.

items.question: What should be done with collective, cyclic, and pedals immediately after touchdown in autorotation?
items.explanation: After touchdown: adjust collective, cyclic, and pedals to control ground run.

items.question: When may the rotor brake be applied after an autorotation landing?
items.explanation: Rotor brake is applied below 170 rpm.

items.question: What is the first step in the in-flight relighting procedure after a flame-out?
items.explanation: The first action is to set the engine starting selector to OFF.

items.question: What is the correct sequence of the first three steps in the in-flight relighting procedure?
options: [FUEL P] ON → Engine starting selector OFF → Engine starting selector ON
Engine starting selector OFF → [FUEL P] ON → Engine starting selector ON
Engine starting selector ON → [FUEL P] ON → Engine starting selector OFF
Twist grip IDLE → [FUEL P] ON → Engine starting selector ON
items.explanation: The correct sequence is OFF, then fuel pump ON, then engine starting selector ON.

items.question: At least how much altitude is required to complete the in-flight relighting procedure?
items.explanation: Manual specifies at least 1000 ft (300 m).

items.question: What are the first two actions if tail rotor thrust is lost while hovering within the HV diagram?
items.explanation: In hover (IGE/OGE within HV diagram): Twist grip → IDLE, Collective → Increase to cushion touchdown.

items.question: What is the first target airspeed to be set when experiencing loss of tail rotor control?
items.explanation: Cyclic and collective are adjusted to set IAS 70 kt in level flight.

items.question: After engaging [HYD TEST] or [ACCU TST], what should be done after 5 seconds?
options: Set collective to full low pitch
Reset [HYD TEST] or [ACCU TST] to OFF
items.explanation: After 5 sec, [HYD TEST] or [ACCU TST] must be reset to OFF.

items.question: What type of landing is recommended after loss of tail rotor control?
options: Shallow approach with a running landing
items.explanation: Manual specifies shallow approach with slight left sideslip, then running landing.

items.question: Which wind condition makes landing easier after loss of tail rotor control?
items.explanation: Manual notes that landing is easier with a RH wind component.

items.question: When the rotor is stopping with wind blowing, how should the aircraft be positioned?
items.explanation: With wind blowing during rotor stopping, position the aircraft head into the wind.

items.question: When the rotor is stopping with wind blowing, how should the cyclic be positioned?
items.explanation: During rotor stopping with wind, the cyclic should be slightly into the wind.

items.question: What is a flight control hardover?
options: A commanded smooth movement of controls
An uncommanded movement of one or two flight controls
A yaw due to tail rotor effectiveness
items.explanation: A hardover results in uncommanded movements of one or two flight controls.

items.question: What is a servojam?
options: A higher than normal force needed to move flight controls
A complete failure of tail rotor control
items.explanation: A servojam results in a higher than normal force required to move the flight controls.

items.question: What immediate action is required during HIGE, Takeoff, or Final if a flight control hardover or servojam occurs?
items.explanation: For HIGE, Takeoff, Final the directive is LAND IMMEDIATELY.

items.question: After landing from a hardover or servojam, which action comes first?
items.explanation: After landing: Hydraulic cut-off switch (collective grip) — OFF.

items.question: During flight with a servojam, which IAS should be set?
items.explanation: In flight: IAS set to between 40 and 60 kt (74 km/h and 111 km/h).

items.question: In flight with servojam, what must be done with the hydraulic cut-off switch?
items.explanation: In flight: Hydraulic cut-off switch (collective grip) — OFF, apply HYDR procedure.

items.question: With no hydraulic pressure, what is noted about aerodynamic loads at high airspeed?
options: They may be heavy and must be counteracted
items.explanation: NOTE: With no hydraulic pressure, the aerodynamic loads to be counteracted may be heavy at high airspeed.

items.question: When the bleed valve opens, what indication appears on the FLI or 3-data page?
items.explanation: When the bleed valve opens, a green 'VV' flag appears on the FLI or 3-data page.

items.question: What is the consequence if the bleed valve flag does not disappear at high power settings (near MCP or above)?
options: Maximum available engine power is reduced, especially in cold weather
The GOV warning light turns off
items.explanation: If the flag does not disappear at high power settings, the maximum available engine power is reduced, specifically in cold weather.

items.question: If the bleed valve flag does not reappear at low power settings, what may occur?
options: The tail rotor may lose thrust
items.explanation: If the flag does not reappear at low power settings, the engine may surge.

items.question: What warning is associated with a bleed valve failure?
items.explanation: A bleed valve failure results in a GOV warning.

items.question: What is the recommended pilot action in case of bleed valve failure?
items.explanation: In case of bleed valve failure, the recommended action is to land as soon as practicable.

items.question: If ICS is inoperative, how will VHF communications be available?
options: Only through COM2 for both pilots
Only for the RH pilot via COM1 transceiver
items.explanation: With ICS inoperative, VHF communications remain available for the RH pilot via COM1 transceiver.

items.question: Where will audio warnings be transmitted if ICS fails?
items.explanation: If ICS fails, audio warnings are transmitted via the COM1 audio system.
